{"id":"a46f4574972e4e98975ae6980220ad10","owner":"MichiganDNR","ownerId":"cbb14257dad7dce9f87613ff5c7a0000","orgId":"Jdnp1TjADvSDxMAX","created":1759344250000,"modified":1788528520000,"guid":null,"name":null,"title":"DNR Managed Sites","type":"Feature Service","typeKeywords":["ArcGIS API for JavaScript","ArcGIS Server","Data","Feature Access","Feature Service","Service","Singlelayer"],"description":"

DNR Managed Sites<\/strong> <\/span>is a comprehensive, statewide geospatial dataset representing physical locations of assets and sites administered or maintained by the Michigan Department of Natural Resources (DNR). Each point feature corresponds to an on-the-ground facility, operational site, recreation feature, or management location that plays a role in delivering DNR programs and services across the state.<\/span><\/p>

This dataset consolidates information from multiple DNR divisions and program areas into a single, standardized asset inventory. It serves as an authoritative reference layer for public transparency, internal planning, maintenance scheduling, recreational access mapping, and cross\u2011divisional coordination.<\/span><\/p>

What the Layer Represents<\/strong><\/span><\/h2>

The features in this layer represent a wide variety of asset types\u2014from parks and recreation sites to fisheries facilities, wildlife management areas, forest management units, harbors, public access sites, and more. Each record includes standardized classification fields that identify:<\/span><\/p>

  • the type of asset (e.g., building, access point, site)<\/span><\/li>
  • a refined detail type for further categorization<\/span><\/li>
  • ownership authority (e.g., DNR division, State, Federal, County, Tribal, or private partner)<\/span><\/li>
  • the specific DNR management unit responsible for administration or maintenance<\/span><\/li>
  • the functional purpose of the site (e.g., Recreation, Forestry, Wildlife, Access, Water, Utility)<\/span><\/li><\/ul>

    These attributes enable users to explore assets by program area, management responsibility, asset purpose, and physical characteristics.<\/span><\/p>

    Rich Attribute Structure for Asset Management<\/strong><\/span><\/h2>

    The layer includes coded value domains for several fields to ensure consistent terminology across DNR programs. Condition ratings enable standardized assessments for planning and maintenance workflows. Functional classifications support program reporting and resource allocation. Surface material categories provide insights into recreation infrastructure and trail/site composition.<\/span><\/p>

    Additional metadata fields record:<\/span><\/p>

    • the method by which each asset was mapped or collected (survey\u2011grade, GNSS, aerial imagery, etc.)<\/span><\/li>
    • the type of edit activity applied during lifecycle management<\/span><\/li>
    • GNSS-derived latitude and longitude<\/span><\/li>
    • automatic editor tracking fields for accountability and version history<\/span><\/li><\/ul>

      This detailed schema supports data reliability and completeness across all DNR asset types.<\/span><\/p>

      Data Collection and Quality<\/strong><\/span><\/h2>

      Records may originate from field inventories, GNSS collection, program-level databases, aerial image interpretation, or historic systems. The Collect Type<\/strong> field indicates the positional accuracy and method used to acquire the spatial location, ranging from high\u2011precision survey data to field-observed or legacy records. The Edit Type<\/strong> field describes how the record has evolved, capturing additions, updates, repositioning, splits, or proposed assets.<\/span><\/p>

      Integration and Cross\u2011Divisional Use<\/strong><\/span><\/h2>

      Because the dataset harmonizes assets from divisions including PRD, WLD, FOD, FRD, Fisheries, Law Enforcement, and the Office of Minerals Management, it acts as a central reference dataset for enterprise-wide DNR mapping. It can be integrated into:<\/span><\/p>

      • public-facing web viewers and recreation maps<\/span><\/li>
      • internal dashboards for park operations, wildlife management, and forestry planning<\/span><\/li>
      • field mobility applications for maintenance crews and site inspection workflows<\/span><\/li>
      • cross\u2011agency coordination, emergency response planning, and resource conservation initiatives<\/span><\/li><\/ul>

        Its consistent schema enables complex spatial queries, thematic mapping, and aggregation of asset information across divisions or geographic service areas.<\/span><\/p>

        Intended Audience and Applications<\/strong><\/span><\/h2>

        The dataset is used by:<\/p>

        • DNR staff for operations, planning, and inventory management<\/span><\/li>
        • Researchers and conservation planners<\/span><\/li>
        • Local governments and partner organizations<\/span><\/li>
        • Members of the public seeking recreation or site information<\/span><\/li>
        • GIS professionals looking for authoritative state-managed asset data<\/span><\/li><\/ul>

          Update Frequency<\/strong><\/span><\/h2>

          The data is actively maintained by DNR GIS staff and division program leads. Editor tracking fields provide timestamps and user information for every change, supporting transparent data stewardship and real-time accuracy improvement.<\/span><\/p>

          Contact Information<\/strong><\/span><\/p>

This spatial data contains Surface Management Agency (SMA, also sometimes called Land Status) information for Idaho from the Idaho Bureau of Land Management (BLM). For federal government lands, this data displays the managing agency of the surface of the land, which does not mean the agency \"owns\" the land. SMA is sometimes referred to as \"ownership\", although this term is inaccurate when describing public lands. This Surface Management Agency data should not be used to depict boundaries (for example National Forest, National Park, National Wildlife Refuge, or Indian Reservation boundaries among others). Attribute information for the federal and private lands are from the BLM Master Title Plats (MTPs), the BLM case files, the BLM Legacy Rehost 2000 (LR2000) database, and corresponding federal Orders and official documents. Please note that because these official sources are strictly used, OTHER NON-BLM FEDERAL AGENCY LANDS MAY NOT BE ATTRIBUTED CORRECTLY unless the proper documents have been filed with the BLM and the land actions have been noted on the MTPs and in LR2000. Starting in the spring of 2011 a field called AGNCY_NAME is present in the data. The AGNCY_NAME field is intended to indicate the managing agency for polygons coded as OTHER in the MGMT_AGNCY field. The AGNCY_NAME field will not be used for the 100K Map Series published by the BLM for use by the public as all agencies in this field are not included in H-1553 Publication Standards Manual Handbook and, therefore, have no BLM Cartographic Standard. Except for polygons coded as OTHER in the MGMT_AGNCY field, all managing agency information in the AGNCY_NAME field should be the same as that of the MGMT_AGNCY field. The only intended difference between the AGNCY_NAME field and the MGMT_AGNCY field is where the MGMT_AGNCY is OTHER. In this case, the AGNCY_NAME will contain an abbreviation for an agency that is not represented in the H-1553 Publication Standards Manual Handbook. Examples of the agencies there are BIA (Bureau of Indian Affairs), USGS (United States Geological Survey), and FAA (Federal Aviation Administration). Attribute information for the State lands is received primarily through cooperation with the Idaho Department of Lands. This information might not reflect all State agency lands completely. A detailed analysis of State owned lands has not been done since June 2011; therefore, recent changes in ownership of State lands may not be reflected. Inclusion of State land information into this dataset is supplemental and should not be viewed as the authoritative source of State lands; please contact State agencies for questions about State lands. This data does not depict land management arrangements between government agencies such as Memorandums of Understanding or other similar agreements. When this data was originally generated in the early 2000's, the primary source of the geometry was the BLM Geographic Coordinate Database (GCDB), if it was available. In areas where GCDB was/is unavailable, the spatial features are taken from a variety of sources including the BLM Idaho Resource Base Data collection, BLM Idaho Master Title Plat AutoCad files, US Geological Survey Digital Line Graphs (DLGs), and US Forest Service Cartographic Feature Files (CFFs), among others (see Process Steps). It should be stressed that the geometry of a feature may not be GCDB-based in the first place, the geometry may shift away from GCDB due to a variety of reasons (topology procedures, automated software processes such as projections, etc.), and the GCDB-based features are not necessarily currently being edited to match improved GCDB. Therefore this data should NOT be considered actual GCDB data. For the latest Idaho GCDB spatial data, please contact the BLM Idaho State Office Cadastral Department at 208-373-4000. The BLM in Idaho creates and maintains this spatial data. This dataset is derived by dissolving based on the \"MGMT_AGNCY\" field from the master SMA GIS dataset (which is edited often) kept by the BLM Idaho State Office. Please get a fresh copy of this data a couple times a year as the SMA data is continually changing. Official actions that affect the managing agency happen often and changes to correct errors are always being made. Nevada SMA data was acquired from the BLM Nevada web site and clipped to the area that is managed by Idaho BLM Boise District. WDFW cartography staff create map content designed to inform map viewers where certain types of recreation opportunities are promoted on WDFW Wildlife Areas. This layer is created from WDFW parcel data using parcel attributes to define where these targeted recreation opportunities exist. There are currently two focused map content areas, one is to support the GoHunt application where hunting opportunities are promoted. The other is used to identify WDFW lands where a Washington Discover Pass is required. The Recreation Access Code, managed in the WDFW_Lands feature class, is used to define which parcels are dissolved into this feature class. Recreation Access Code values that are brought across as a result of a standard definition query are: 1 - Parcels managed within a designated Wildlife Area and not restricted in any way for being displayed on GoHunt or Discover Pass maps; 4 - Parcels designated by the Wildlife Program for exclusion from GoHunt activities; 5 - Parcels designated by the Wildlife Program for exclusion from the Discover Pass. Users of this feature class can use ArcMap definition queries to appropriately display either GoHunt or Discover Pass map content. This feature class displays the finest scale of the Wildlife Area administrative hierarchy that consists of Widlife Area Complexes, Wildlife Areas and Wildlife Area Units. {"id":"d296b58b0eae485fba2c55ab90e5908d","owner":"WA_RCO_Admin","ownerId":"fcb34a47ff3ddb8c523eacab80cc7e89","orgId":"TGEC20q86HQAeMS6","created":1559327493000,"modified":1771527835000,"guid":null,"name":"Public_Lands_Inventory_2","title":"WA RCO Public Lands Inventory 2019","type":"Feature Service","typeKeywords":["ArcGIS Server","Data","Feature Access","Feature Service","Metadata","Service","Singlelayer","Hosted Service"],"description":"

The WA RCO Public Lands Inventory 2019 layer supports the Public Lands Inventory required by the <\/span>2017-19 Capital Budget, Chapter 2, Laws of 2018, Section 3083, (SSB 6090)<\/span><\/a>, which tasked the Recreation and Conservation Office (RCO) to update the public lands inventory with current information on state agency habitat and recreation land acquisitions and easements and to further develop the inventory to respond to the <\/span>recommendations<\/span><\/a> of the Joint Legislative Audit and Review Committee for creating a single source of information about land acquisitions. <\/span><\/p>

The 2019 update to the Public Lands Inventory must include updated parcel data for state and federal lands and will retain all of the Public Lands Inventory 2014 elements below. Per the 2015 Joint Legislative Audit Review Committee (JLARC) final report on State Recreation and Habitat Lands, it must also: <\/span><\/p>

·<\/span> <\/span><\/span><\/span>Provide details about acquisition and funding <\/span><\/p>

o<\/span> <\/span><\/span><\/span>Provide details about the properties proposed for acquisition, including location, acreage, and current use. <\/span><\/p>

o<\/span> <\/span><\/span><\/span>Estimated acquisition cost and fund source(s). <\/span><\/p>

o<\/span> <\/span><\/span><\/span>Include all proposed acquisitions, regardless of fund source(s). <\/span><\/p>

o<\/span> <\/span><\/span><\/span>Include all land disposals. <\/span><\/p>

·<\/span> <\/span><\/span><\/span>Link proposed or new acquisitions to plans and detailed outcomes <\/span><\/p>

o<\/span> <\/span><\/span><\/span>Explain how the acquisition relates to the agency\u2019s plans for an entire management unit (i.e., state park, wildlife area, or natural area) <\/span><\/p>

o<\/span> <\/span><\/span><\/span>Clearly identify the detailed outcomes for the property and entire management unit such as specific development plans, service improvements, staffing levels, or habitat restoration needs. <\/span><\/p>

o<\/span> <\/span><\/span><\/span>Clearly describe agency progress toward achieving the detailed outcomes and how the acquisition helps achieve those outcomes. <\/span><\/p>

·<\/span> <\/span><\/span><\/span>Identify future costs to achieve and maintain detailed outcomes <\/span><\/p>

o<\/span> <\/span><\/span><\/span>Estimate future capital, operating, and maintenance costs for the entire management unit, including the costs to achieve the detailed outcomes. <\/span><\/p>

o<\/span> <\/span><\/span><\/span>Explain how the proposed acquisition affects those estimated costs. <\/span><\/p>

<\/span><\/p>

In addition to the requirements outlined above, the Recreation and Conservation Office has set the following requirements for the Public Lands Inventory: <\/span><\/p>

·<\/span> <\/span><\/span><\/span>Create an open data service, where state agencies will provide their ownership data and other information described above and include enhanced reporting of forecast and monitoring information and the ability to view/sort data as needed. o Expand reporting capabilities to allow end users to generate and print their own ownership reports by geographic boundaries and data ranges. <\/span><\/p>

<\/span><\/p>

The WA RCO Public Lands Inventory 2014 layer supports the 2013-15 Capital Budget, Chapter 19, Laws of 2013, Section 3174, (ESSB 5035) tasked the Recreation and Conservation Office (RCO) to provide a centralized inventory of lands in Washington owned by federal, state and local governments, and by Native American tribes.
